chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to me, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'adah ibn Sadaqah, who said:

Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) was asked about the narration that came from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'The noblest jihad is to say a word of justice in front of an oppressive ruler.' What is its meaning? He replied: 'This is on the condition that he commands him to the extent of his knowledge, and in that case it is accepted from him; otherwise, no.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith 'The noblest jihad is a word of justice before an oppressive ruler'?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'noblest jihad' of speaking truth to an unjust ruler is conditional upon the ruler's capacity to accept the advice, highlighting the Shia principle of balancing truthfulness with wisdom (hikmah) to avoid futile conflict. This interpretation underscores that the spiritual merit lies in the sincere effort of admonition within one's means, rather than the immediate political outcome. It reflects the scholarly tradition of distinguishing between the obligation of enjoining good and the practical constraints of the era.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-16 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted on the authority of Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Mus’adat ibn Sadaqah:

Ja’far ibn Muhammad was questioned about the meaning of a narration on the authority of the Prophet (MGB) that says, “The noblest holy war is to say just words in front of an oppressive ruler.” He replied, ‘It means that he should instruct him to do as much as he can understand. This much effort is accepted from him. He has no more duties.’”
